title: Obokano (box lyre)
summary: The obokano is the big box lyre of the Gusii people of Kenya. Its body is a large square wooden box with a carved window, two stout posts rise from it to a thick crossbar, and eight strings run from large leather rings down to the box. The sound is deep and humming.
howToPlay: Eight strings run from the big rings on the crossbar to the bridge, the lowest on the left. Each lane marks a place to pluck a string.
Beads slide down the strings. Pluck the lane as the bead lands.
The tunes are slow and deep, with long notes that ring on.
Let each note ring before the next, and keep the pulse steady.
rules: The eight strings are tuned to a five-note minor scale spread over two octaves.
A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Songs count four beats to the bar at a slow pace.
heritageNote: The obokano is played in the Gusii highlands of western Kenya as a solo instrument for slow, deep songs. Its large box gives it a humming, drone-like voice, and its thick crossbar and big rings are made to carry heavy strings.
